newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks moderately lower in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks moderately lower in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks slipped lower in early Tuesday morning trade with little news to simulated institutional interest, although downside appeared limited, brokers said.
"In the short term, the market is going nowhere, said Archie Hart, director of BZW Securities Asia. "We will need some exceptional corporate results...or good news out of China to get us going."
The Hang Seng Index shed 48 points to 13,594 on turnover of moderate HK$ 1.40 billion. The index touched a low of 13,557.20 shortly after the open but rebounded on rising turnover.
"If it hadn't been for Hongkong Bank (HSBC Holdings), we would have been down a 100 points yesterday," said Hart.
HSBC, which accounts for about 18 percent of the Hang Seng Index, soared HK$5.50 to close at HK$189.50 on Monday, while the Hang Seng Index eased 16.96 points to 13,643.54.
Brokers said it looked as though some big local players were taking a bearish position and shorting futures.
The Hang Seng Index February futures contract was trading 45 points lower at 13,515 and the March contract 70 points lower at 13,510, both a discount to the cash market.
Selling in property shares led the market down. The commercial and industrials sector was also weak. Most H shares and red chips were relatively unchanged.

Sun Hung Kai Properties led the sector down, with a fall of HK$1.75 to HK$89.25, followed by Henderson Land which was sold off HK$0.75 to 70.75. New World Development also eased HK$0.50, but New World Infrastructure added HK$0.05 to HK$22.95.

CITIC Pacific lost HK$0.50 to HK$38.80. The company announced that it had completed the purchase of 199.06 million new China Light shares, the tranche of its acquisition of a 20 percent stake in the utility.

China Light was unchanged at HK$36.70. "The share is ex-growth in Hong Kong ...and fundamentally, it is a sell but if you take a longer term view there are some interesting angles looking at the stock," said BZW's Hart.
H shares were gnerally little changed. But Qingling Motors continued its bull run, adding HK$0.20 to HK$4.375, while Guangdong Kelon slumped HK$0.15 to HK$6.20.

"Red chips are still attractive," said Allen Pao in institutional sales at South China Securities. "But they are now digesting 1996 gains and recent share placements. China Resources eased HK$0.25 to HK$16.20.
